userStories.title: Degrade the root run-start baseline per command
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make an unparseable failing root test command degrade the baseline even when a sibling names failures.

**Motivation** — With `quality.commands.test: ["cmd-a", "cmd-b"]`, where `cmd-a` names one failure and `cmd-b` fails naming none, the baseline is `captured` with only `cmd-a`'s entry; every pre-existing `cmd-b` failure is later labelled `introduced`.

**Approach** — `captureRunBaselineInner` replaces `aggregateUnparseableFailure(outcome)` with `unparseableFailure(outcome)`: the first command, in run order, that failed and whose own parse named no failure makes the baseline `unparseable` with that command's evidence. `aggregateUnparseableFailure` is deleted. Everything else on the root path is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: root capture's helper import/call, deletion of the obsolete helper and stale aggregate-rule comments, evidence fixtures and info logging assertions. Out: chat launch protection (US-002), agent discovery (US-003), transcript/footer changes (US-004), queue steering (US-005) and Esc/mouse handling (US-006). `.nax/` files are not edited by this feature's stories; `.nax/features/run-start-baseline-fixes/spec.md` US-004 ("runs exactly as today") was updated by hand on this branch before the run.

**Interface** — Reuse `unparseableFailure(outcome)`, `evidenceFor(run)` and `writeNoBaseline` without changing their contracts. Removal of `aggregateUnparseableFailure` is verified by the normal build/static gate, `bun run typecheck`.

**Regression update** — In `packages/nax/test/unit/execution/lifecycle/test-baseline-capture-evidence.test.ts`, replace the test "AC4: a named failure anywhere in the root command list keeps the baseline captured" with the same cmd-a/cmd-b fixture expecting exactly one `no-baseline` marker, `reason: "unparseable"` and `evidence.command: "cmd-b"`; remove its preceding aggregate-rule comment. Preserve timeout/error precedence, per-package behavior and evidence redaction.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] captureRunBaseline with _captureDeps.resolveTestCommands returning ["cmd-a", "cmd-b"], both commands failing, cmd-a parsing to one named failure and cmd-b parsing to failed: 4 with no named failure, writes exactly one baseline: kind: "no-baseline", reason: "unparseable", evidence.command equal to cmd-b.

[unit] captureRunBaseline with commands ["cmd-a", "cmd-b", "cmd-c"], all failing, cmd-a and cmd-b each naming one failure and cmd-c naming none, writes a no-baseline marker whose evidence.command is cmd-c.

[unit] captureRunBaseline with commands ["cmd-a", "cmd-b"], cmd-a failing with one named failure { file: "a.test.ts", testName: "fails" } and cmd-b succeeding with no failures, writes one captured baseline whose entries equal [{ file: "a.test.ts", testName: "fails" }].
[unit] captureRunBaseline with one command that fails and names no failure writes a no-baseline marker with reason: "unparseable" and evidence.command equal to that command.

[unit] captureRunBaseline with commands ["cmd-a", "cmd-b"], both failing, cmd-a naming one failure and cmd-b naming none, logs one info entry at stage execution whose data has reason: "unparseable" and command: "cmd-b".

routing.reasoning: A small two-module behavior correction and existing fixture update using established capture/evidence seams; no new abstraction or security-sensitive session path.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "AC4: a named failure anywhere in the root command list keeps the baseline captured" pins the aggregate rule this story removes (`cmd-a` names one failure, `cmd-b` fails naming none, expected one `captured` write with no evidence); it becomes a test that the same fixture writes one `no-baseline` marker with reason `unparseable` and `evidence.command` equal to `cmd-b`, and its preceding comment about the aggregate rule is removed.

userStories.title: Refuse chat plan and run launches on protected branches
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse chat plan/run launches and chain proposals on main, master or an exit-zero unnamed branch before approval or execution.

**Motivation** — A chat agent launched `nax-jobs__run` with the checkout on `main`, and the run committed onto `main`.

**Approach** — A new exported function in `chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts`:

```ts
// packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts
export async function featureBranchRefusal(input: {
  readonly kind: "plan" | "run";
  readonly feature: string;
  readonly repoRoot: string;
}): Promise<string | undefined>;
```

It reads the checked-out branch with `_jobsLaunchDeps.git(["symbolic-ref", "--short", "HEAD"], repoRoot)` (the call `launchReason` already makes). When that call exits non-zero (detached HEAD, not a repository), it returns `undefined`: the branch is unknown and the launch is not refused. When the trimmed branch fails `isPublishableBranch(branch)` (`utils/git.ts`: `""`, `main`, `master`), it returns the refusal text:

```
[chat] nax <kind> for <feature> refused: the checkout is on <branch>; plan and run a feature on its feature branch <target>. Create or check out <target>, then launch again.
```

`<branch>` is the branch name, or `an unnamed branch` for `""`. `<target>` is the feature PRD's `branchName` when `<featureDir>/prd.json` exists and loads (through `_jobsLaunchDeps.exists` and `_jobsLaunchDeps.loadPRD`), otherwise `feat/<feature>` (the planner's default, `plan/strategies/context-builder.ts`). No default-branch lookup is made.

Call sites:
- `launchJob`: after `prepareTarget` and `unknownWorkflowProfile` succeed and before the busy check, a `plan` or `run` input whose `featureBranchRefusal` returns text ends the call with `{ isError: true, content: <text> }`; no approval is requested and no job starts. This covers chain auto-admission too, since it runs inside `launchJob`.
- `chain-tools.ts` `resolveStepTarget`: a `plan` or `run` step whose `featureBranchRefusal` returns text yields that step's error through `stepError(step, text)`, so no chain card is shown.

`buildWorkflowInstructions` (`prompts/builders/workflow-builder.ts`) gains one fixed line, placed after `pathsLine()` and before the optional lines:

```
A feature's `nax plan` and `nax run` happen on its feature branch (the PRD's branchName, by default feat/<feature>), never on main or master: create or check out that branch before the launch; `nax-jobs__plan` and `nax-jobs__run` refuse on main, master or an unnamed branch.
```

**Scope** — In: shared branch refusal helper, both launch and chain-step wiring, exact workflow guidance and launch/chain regressions. Out: baseline classification (US-001), resource discovery/builtins (US-003), UI footer/queue/Esc changes (US-004–US-006). The `nax run` CLI does not check or switch branches; only the chat launch tools refuse. The default branch read from `origin/HEAD` is not consulted by the launch guard; only `""`, `main` and `master` are refused. A launch on a detached HEAD is not refused. `nax-jobs__finish`, `nax-jobs__bot_review` and `nax-jobs__bot_fix` are not guarded by branch; publish keeps `auto-pr`'s own guard.

**Interface** — `featureBranchRefusal(input: { readonly kind: "plan" | "run"; readonly feature: string; readonly repoRoot: string; }): Promise<string | undefined>` as declared above; reuse `isPublishableBranch(branch, defaultBranch?)`, `featureDir(repoRoot, feature)` and `_jobsLaunchDeps` without bypassing target preparation or approval ordering.

**Regression updates** — Change only the main-answering git stubs in `jobs-launch-chain.test.ts`, `jobs-launch-nested.test.ts`, `jobs-launch-busy.test.ts` and `chain-tools-repo.test.ts` to feat/f1, keeping every other assertion. In `workflow-builder.test.ts`, introduce the exact BRANCH_LINE and change `[PATHS_LINE, CHOICES_LINE]` to `[PATHS_LINE, BRANCH_LINE, CHOICES_LINE]`; keep the original-line prefix and approval-wording assertions. Create the branch test file listed in expectedFiles.

Create or check out feat/f1-x, then launch again.".

userStories.title: Load nax user agents and always expose built-in explore
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace Claude user-agent discovery with nax user agents and make general/explore invocable even with an empty catalog.

**Motivation** — Those agents are written for Claude Code, and they land in every nax chat's `nax-agents__run` listing.

**Approach** — `discoverClaudeCodePackages` keeps scanning `~/.claude` for skills, commands, settings, hooks and MCP, but the `claude-user` package no longer scans `<claudeDir>/agents`: its `agents` is `[]`. The repo's `.claude/agents/` (`claude-project`) and enabled Claude plugins' agents are unchanged.

A new `ResourceOrigin` kind `{ kind: "nax-user" }` labels agents from `naxAgentsDir(env)/*.md`. `naxAgentsDir(env)` is a new export of `resources/claude-paths.ts`: `join(env.NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(_claudePathsDeps.homedir(), ".nax"), "agents")` — the same override and default as `globalConfigDir()`, read from the `env` that `loadResourceCatalog` is given rather than from `process.env`. The directory is scanned with `scanAgentsDir` into a package with id `nax-user`; the package is left out of the catalog when it holds no agents and no diagnostics (an absent directory yields neither). `loadResourceCatalog` loads it whether or not `resources.claudeCode` is enabled, and orders packages `[claude-project, nax-user, claude-user, …claude plugins, …nax plugins]`, so on a name clash a repo agent wins over a `~/.nax` agent, which wins over a plugin agent. `originLabel` returns `nax-user` for it.

`chat/builtin-agent.ts` gains `explore`:

```ts
export const EXPLORE_AGENT_NAME = "explore";
export function exploreAgent(): AgentResource; // tools ["Read", "Glob", "Grep", "Git"], origin nax-builtin, no model
```

`agentNamed(catalog, name)` resolves a catalog agent first, then the `general` and `explore` built-ins. `explore`'s prompt comes from a new `buildExploreAgentPrompt()` in `prompts/builders/agents-builder.ts` (read-only search: find and read code, report file paths and line numbers, change nothing), and its description is a new `EXPLORE_AGENT_DESCRIPTION` in `builtin-agent.ts`: `Searches and reads the codebase without changing it`.

The agent-facing text names `explore` in the sentence that already names `general`, so neither the instruction line count nor the overflow line moves: the sentence `For read-only code search, pass agent explore: it has Read, Glob, Grep and Git only.` is appended to `buildAgentsInstructions`'s third line and to the end of `RUN_DESCRIPTION` (`agents-provider.ts`). `createAgentsProvider` always offers the `run` tool and always returns instructions (the three fixed lines, then any catalog entries). The host attaches `nax-agents` whether or not the catalog has agents (`chat-host.ts`). `/agents` (`chat-agents-listing.ts`) stays a listing of catalog agents only.

**Scope** — In: origin/path/catalog discovery and precedence, skip claude-user agent scanning, builtin explore, builder/barrel wiring, always-on agents provider for resource-enabled hosts, and affected provider/order fixtures. Out: launch branch protection (US-002), baseline behavior (US-001), footer and key handling (US-004–US-006). Skills, commands, settings, hooks and MCP from `~/.claude` are still loaded; only `~/.claude/agents/` stops. The repo's `.claude/agents/` and Claude plugin agents are still loaded. `/agents` does not list the built-in `general` and `explore` agents. A long subagent run is not kept alive past its parent turn's end, nor moved to a background task (#2930 second half stays open).

**Interface** — `export const EXPLORE_AGENT_NAME = "explore"; export function exploreAgent(): AgentResource;` as above; add `{ readonly kind: "nax-user" }` to `ResourceOrigin`, export `naxAgentsDir(env)` from `resources/claude-paths.ts`, and add `buildExploreAgentPrompt()` to the prompt builder surface. `EXPLORE_AGENT_DESCRIPTION` is exactly `Searches and reads the codebase without changing it`. Reuse the existing run callback and tool-mapping policy, not a new dispatch path.

**Failure behavior** — An absent nax agents directory creates neither a package nor a diagnostic. A malformed file produces the existing scanAgentsDir diagnostic and retains a diagnostics-only package.

**Regression updates** — Replace agents-provider.test.ts's empty-catalog no-tool/undefined-instruction assertions with one run tool and three fixed instruction lines, and append the explore sentence to its exact description/suffix constants and agents-builder.test.ts's third-line expectation. Update host provider ordering in chat-host-tasks.test.ts, host-subagents.test.ts, chat-host-jobs.test.ts and chat-host-resources.test.ts to end in nax-tasks then nax-agents after the existing resources/optional jobs providers. In resources/catalog.test.ts, pass a temp NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR alongside CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to prevent developer-home reads, leaving assertions unchanged. New tests are listed in expectedFiles; keep builtins outside the catalog.

When a nax agents directory contains only malformed agent files, loadResourceCatalog retains the nax-user package and its diagnostics.
naxAgentsDir({}) returns the agents directory under the injected home directory's .nax folder.

userStories.title: Center transcript markers and group footer shells
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Center transcript bottom markers, compact running shells into one footer part and open a lone shell's output on a strip click.

**Motivation** — Each running background command is its own `bash <command>` footer part (`formatJobStrip`), so a few shells crowd the strip.

**Approach** — The marker row in `TranscriptViewport.tsx` is centred in the viewport width (`justifyContent="center"` on the row), still truncated when wider than the window; `markerRowAt` keeps hit-testing the whole row. `formatJobStrip`, `FooterJob` and `FooterTask` stay in `chat-status.ts`; the per-task `taskPart` is removed. `chat-status.ts` is at 600 lines and `check:file-sizes` rejects a 601-line source file, so the rewritten strip must leave the file at or under 600 lines, with room for US-005's one new hint entry. The strip is: up to `JOB_STRIP_LIMIT` (2) job parts, then ` +<k>` for hidden jobs, then — when tasks run — the separator ` · ` and one part `1 shell` or `<n> shells` (for example `run a · run b +1 · 1 shell`). `use-jobs-opener.ts`: a left press and release on the footer strip reads, at click time, the running tasks from `host.tasks?.list()` and the running jobs from `host.jobs?.list()`. With exactly one running task and no running job it calls the new input `showOutput(taskEntry(task, now))` — the same listing Enter on that task's jobs-picker row produces, titled `bash <command> · running` — and opens no picker; otherwise it opens the jobs picker as today. ctrl+g always opens the jobs picker, so a lone shell can still be stopped there with ctrl+x. `useChatPicker` returns its existing `showOutput`, and `picker-model.ts` exports its existing `taskEntry`. The fitted footer's `N active (ctrl+g)` fallback (`status-layout.ts`) keeps counting each task.

**Scope** — In: marker layout only, shell grouping and widths, exposing picker output/task-entry APIs, ChatApp callback wiring and event-time click routing. Out: queued hint/ctrl+s behavior (US-005), Esc confirmation/mouse buffering (US-006), baseline/launch/resource changes (US-001–US-003). Part-level hit-testing inside the footer strip is not added: a click anywhere on the strip acts on the whole strip. ctrl+g keeps opening the jobs picker in every case; only a strip click opens a lone shell directly. The fitted footer's `N active (ctrl+g)` fallback keeps counting each task and each job.

**Interface** — Preserve `formatJobStrip(jobs, tasks)` in `chat-status.ts`. `useJobsOpener` input gains `showOutput(entry: PickerEntry): void`; `useChatPicker`'s return gains its existing `showOutput(entry: PickerEntry): Promise<void>`; `taskEntry(task, nowMs)` is exported unchanged.

**Regression updates** — Replace per-command strip text in chat-status-tasks.test.ts with 1 shell/N shells after jobs; remove strip command-elision/newline cases and measure new strip widths. footer-tasks.test.tsx AC-14 expects 1 shell while running and no shell part after completion. jobs-opener.test.tsx changes STRIP to 1 shell; the first-column and last-column lone-task clicks expect the bash <command> · running transcript listing and no picker title. Preserve AC-12–AC-17 no-action assertions and AC-6/AC-18/AC-19/AC-20 ctrl+g assertions. New rendered tests live in footer-shells.test.tsx. Do not center ordinary transcript rows.

userStories.title: Send the oldest queued message now with ctrl+s
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let ctrl+s on an empty prompt steer the oldest queued message into the running turn and advertise that gesture.

**Motivation** — A line typed during a turn is queued (`queued · <text>` rows), but nothing can send a queued line now: ctrl+s steers only the typed draft, and no hint names it.

**Approach** — `steerRunningTurn` in `ChatApp.tsx`: when a turn is sending, the draft is empty (its text trims to `""`), no interrupt send is pending (`interruptSend.current === undefined`), and the queue is non-empty, the oldest queued line is taken off the queue (`takeQueued`) and handed to the running turn exactly as a typed line would be (steer when the brain accepts, else interrupt and send next). With an interrupt send already pending, ctrl+s on an empty draft does nothing: the queue drains behind that send. A slash-line draft is not empty and keeps today's behaviour (ctrl+s does nothing). `footerHint` (`use-clipboard-feedback.ts`) takes a new optional `queued?: boolean` input (absent means `false`, so existing callers and fixtures that omit it keep today's result); when the turn is busy, no layer owns esc, and `queued` is true, it returns the new `FixedHint` `"queued"` (gesture `esc to interrupt`, extra `ctrl+s to send queued now`), ahead of `background`. `queued` is true when the queue is non-empty, the draft trims to `""`, and no interrupt send is pending.

**Scope** — In: queued-line selection through the existing steering/interrupt path, ref-safe queue removal, new queued hint and footer eligibility. Out: shell strip/marker layout and click routing (US-004), Esc confirmation and split mouse handling (US-006), baseline/branch/resource changes (US-001–US-003). Preserve typed-draft priority, slash-line no-op, existing image refusal and normal queue-drain behavior.

**Interface** — `footerHint` input gains optional `queued?: boolean` (absent = `false`); `FooterHint`/`FixedHint`/`HINT_PARTS` gain `"queued"` with gesture `esc to interrupt` and extra `ctrl+s to send queued now`. Reuse `takeQueued(queue)` and its existing atomic `{ text, rest }` result; no new queue API or host dispatch method.

**Dependency and tests** — Depends on US-004 because removing taskPart frees room for the hint in chat-status.ts at its 600-line hard limit. Add chat-steer-queued.test.tsx for rendered queue/steering/interrupt and footer observations. Existing steering tests use nonempty drafts and existing footer tests have empty queues; retain their behavioral assertions. Update required footerHint input fixtures with queued:false if needed without changing expectations. The unsupported-steer fallback still interrupts immediately; US-006's Esc confirmation must not later gate that programmatic path.

userStories.title: Confirm destructive Esc
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Require a second timely Esc to stop a turn or stopping question.

**Motivation** — A single Esc stops the turn (`ChatApp.tsx` `host.cancel()`, and `dismissQuestion` for a session question).

**Approach** — A new `tui/chat/esc-confirm.ts` exports `ESC_CONFIRM_MS = 2_000` and a hook `useEscConfirm()` returning `{ armed: boolean; press(): boolean }`: `press()` returns `true` when it follows an armed press by less than `ESC_CONFIRM_MS` (read through `_chatKeyDeps.now`, exclusive like ctrl+c's `DOUBLE_INTERRUPT_MS`), and otherwise arms and returns `false`; a timer armed through a new `_escConfirmDeps = { setTimeout, clearTimeout }` clears `armed` (and so the hint) when the window passes. `press()` decides from the arm time held in a ref it writes synchronously, never from the rendered `armed`, so two Escapes delivered in one input batch with no render between them still confirm. The arm is also cleared when the turn ends and when the top Esc layer changes (for example a question card replacing the bare turn), so a new turn or a different layer never inherits it. Esc on the `turn` layer, and Esc on a `question` layer with `stops: true`, call `host.cancel()` / `dismissQuestion` only when `press()` returns `true`. `escHintText(layer, armed)` returns `esc again to interrupt` for an armed `turn` layer and `esc again to close and stop` for an armed stopping question; unarmed hints are unchanged. Every other Esc layer (approval, choice, non-stopping question, picker, menu, idle clear) keeps its single Esc. ctrl+c is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: new confirmation hook and lifecycle reset, destructive Esc wiring, armed hints, and deterministic timer tests. Out: split mouse-prefix handling (US-007), queue selection/hint eligibility (US-005), shell grouping/clicks (US-004), baseline/branch/resource changes (US-001–US-003). A long subagent run is not kept alive past its parent turn's end, nor moved to a background task (#2930 second half stays open). The native adapter's whole-turn deadline and idle watchdog aborts (`native/session-adapter.ts`) keep aborting with no reason; the ACP twin of the abandoned message is unchanged. ctrl+c still cancels a running turn on its first press. Approval, choice, non-stopping question, picker and menu layers keep a single Esc.

**Interface** — `useEscConfirm()` returns `{ armed: boolean; press(): boolean }`; `ESC_CONFIRM_MS = 2_000`; `_escConfirmDeps = { setTimeout, clearTimeout }`; `escHintText(layer, armed = false)`. Reuse `_chatKeyDeps.now`, `topEscLayer`. Reset confirmation on turn end and top-layer changes without making same-batch presses rely on a rendered state. Keep immediate programmatic cancellation (including unsupported steering) outside this Esc-only guard.

**Regression updates** — chat-app-keys.test.tsx AC-1 and chat-app-esc-layers.test.tsx AC-1/AC-15/AC-4 now press Escape twice but retain one cancel and the existing decline-before-cancel order. chat-steering-host.test.tsx B2 changes its single batch to ["hi", RETURN, ESCAPE, ESCAPE], preserving the live-claim assertion. New files are listed in expectedFiles; drive dependency clocks/timers, not real waits. Depends on US-005 because both change ChatApp footer hint composition.

userStories.title: Buffer split mouse-report prefixes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prevent a mouse report split after its first bytes from reaching Ink as a lone Escape.

**Motivation** — Chat enables any-motion mouse tracking (`ENABLE_MOUSE`), and `filterReports` holds back a split report only once its `\u001b[<` prefix is complete, so a read that ends after `\u001b` or `\u001b[` hands Ink a lone Escape, which Ink reports as `key.escape` (#2930).

**Approach** — `mouse-input.ts` holds a trailing `\u001b` or `\u001b[` at the end of a chunk as pending. When the next chunk continues it into `\u001b[<…`, the report is parsed as today; when it continues with anything else, the held bytes are forwarded ahead of it; when no data arrives within `ESC_FLUSH_MS = 50`, the held bytes are forwarded alone, so a real Esc press reaches Ink 50 ms later. The flush timer runs through a new exported `_mouseInputDeps = { setTimeout, clearTimeout }`; new data, the flush itself and `dispose()` each clear a pending timer.

**Scope** — In: split-prefix hold/flush in `mouse-input.ts` and deterministic timer tests. Out: Esc confirmation (US-006) and every other chat change.

**Interface** — `ESC_FLUSH_MS = 50`; `_mouseInputDeps = { setTimeout, clearTimeout }`. Keep the existing `MouseInput` and Ink stream contracts.

**Regression updates** — mouse-input.test.ts's AC-13/AC-22 cases for lone Escape and Escape-[ now assert no forwarded bytes before the injected flush callback and the same bytes after it. Preserve full-report inline text, broken grammar and bounded-partial-buffer behavior. Drive the injected timers, not real waits.
